content.text: The Full Picture Most Guides Leave Out: Notion templates

Most guides will tell you to use Gumroad or Payhip to sell your Notion templates, but they'll leave out the fact that these platforms take a significant cut of your earnings, leaving you with less than half of what you could be making. However, with a sovereign digital commerce stack, you can keep 100% of your earnings, and with NOWPayments, you can process payments in cryptocurrencies like USDT and Bitcoin, which have lower transaction fees compared to traditional payment methods. This means you can sell more, and keep more of what you earn, without breaking the bank. By building a sovereign digital commerce stack, you can say goodbye to platform fees and hello to higher earnings and greater flexibility.
Every Component and What It Does

A sovereign digital commerce stack consists of several key components, including a hosting platform, a backend logic layer, an order storage system, a file delivery system, and a payment processing system. With GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, you can host your Notion templates for free, while Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script can handle the backend logic. Supabase or Google Sheets can store orders, and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 can deliver files. NOWPayments can process payments, giving you the flexibility to accept payments in cryptocurrencies like USDT and Bitcoin. Each component plays a crucial role in ensuring that your digital commerce stack runs smoothly and efficiently.
The Technical Layer Explained Without Abstraction

The technical layer of your sovereign digital commerce stack is where the magic happens. With Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, you can create custom functions and triggers to automate tasks, such as sending order confirmations and delivering files. You can also use APIs to integrate with other services, like email marketing software or customer support platforms. The technical layer is where you can get creative and build custom solutions to meet your specific needs. By leveraging the power of cloud-based services, you can build a scalable and secure digital commerce stack that can handle high traffic and large sales volumes.
Selling digital products globally has never been easier with a sovereign digital commerce stack.
Edge Cases, Failures, and How to Handle Them

No digital commerce stack is perfect, and there will always be edge cases and failures. However, with a sovereign digital commerce stack, you can mitigate these risks by building redundancy and fail-safes into your system. For example, you can use a load balancer to distribute traffic across multiple servers, and a content delivery network (CDN) to cache frequently requested resources. You can also use monitoring and logging tools to detect issues before they become major problems. By being proactive and anticipating potential failures, you can ensure that your digital commerce stack runs smoothly and efficiently, even in the face of unexpected challenges.
The Complete Deployment Roadmap

Deploying a sovereign digital commerce stack requires careful planning and execution. First, you need to choose a hosting platform and set up your backend logic layer. Next, you need to configure your order storage system and file delivery system. Finally, you need to integrate your payment processing system and test everything to ensure that it works as expected.
